title: Thinking ahead: inputs, caching and reuse
intro: Catch up on the key A Level ideas. Complete four retrieval questions, work through the examples, then practise and explain your reasoning.

questions.prompt: Why is caching squares safer than caching changing attendance data?
questions.answer: Squares of the same integer do not change; attendance does.
options: Squares of the same integer do always change; attendance does.
Squares of the same integer do not change; attendance does.
Squares of the different integer do not change; attendance does.
questions.feedback: Model answer: Squares of the same integer do not change; attendance does.

blocks.title: Key vocabulary
items: input — Data passed into a computation.
precondition — Condition required before a process can run correctly.
cache hit — Requested value found in storage.
cache invalidation — Removing or refreshing outdated stored results.

blocks.title: Define the contract
blocks.text: The input is an integer, and the output is its square; overflow is a possible precondition concern.

blocks.title: Trace repeated work
blocks.text: First call for 5 calculates and caches 25; second returns the stored result.

blocks.title: Evaluate caching
blocks.text: Saves repeated calculation but costs memory. For changing data, cached values can become out of date.

blocks.title: Worked example · Predict first
blocks.text: The key A is already stored, so the lookup uses the cache.

blocks.title: Worked example · Model and check
blocks.text: If pricing changes, the cached price must be updated or expired.
